slides.title: 5 pieces of good news you might have missed
slides.body: Real stories from this week's science pages. No doom, just quiet progress.

slides.title: Nature as a flood wall
slides.body: Mangroves and forests can protect against floods, droughts and rising seas, and they adapt as the climate changes. In some countries it has proved cheaper than concrete and steel.

slides.title: A patch for deeper sleep
slides.body: A wearable patch using gentle ultrasound helped people reach REM sleep sooner and stay in it longer in early tests. No pills, no surgery.

slides.title: Faster blades for Mars
slides.body: NASA tested helicopter blades at very high speeds in a chamber that mimics the Martian air. More lift could mean future helicopters carry more kit and fly further.

slides.title: A helpful gut sugar
slides.body: Scientists found a sugar made by a gut bacterium that helped burn visceral fat, the kind around our organs, and improved metabolic health. Early research, but promising.

slides.title: A protein that guards the brain
slides.body: In mice, boosting one protein reduced the toxic tau tangles linked to Alzheimer's, and brain shrinkage. Removing it made the damage worse.

slides.title: Which one made your day?
slides.body: Comment the number 1–5. And save this for a gloomy morning.
